The short answer: the Dreame Pocket Pro at about C$160 is the joint-highest-rated dryer above C$120 in our entire Canadian dataset at 4.6★ from 252 ratings, and it is one of the very few high-speed dryers sold in Canada that is genuinely dual voltage. It includes a diffuser, and it sells through a brand-operated listing with a single seller. The honest limitation is volume. At roughly 163 units a month in Canada, there are not yet enough long-term owners to say anything confident about how it behaves in year three. We have also not bench-tested it, so what follows separates what we can verify from what we cannot.

What we liked about the Dreame Pocket Pro

1. It is the joint-highest-rated dryer above C$120 in our dataset at 4.6★. That is measured against 334 reviews in the over-C$120 band. Only the Laifen Air Diffuser matches it, and it does so at a lower price Amazon.ca data.

2. Dual voltage is genuinely rare here. Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 785 mentions — ahead of noise, weight and price. Most Canadian dryers are 120V only, so a high-speed dryer that works abroad is a real functional advantage rather than a specification nicety Review analysis.

3. A diffuser that is matched to the dryer. Attachment security generated 186 mentions in our dataset with 57% negative, and the recurring complaint is parts falling off. A diffuser that ships with the dryer is sized to its barrel and holds better than a universal aftermarket part Review analysis.

4. Brand-operated listing with a single seller. The Buy Box is held by Dreame Technology HK with no competing sellers. Warranty and service complaints were the second-largest cluster in our data at 610 negative mentions and an 81% negative share, and a large part of that comes from reseller listings where nobody owns the claim. This listing avoids that Amazon.ca data.

5. It sits in the price band where complaints fall sharply. Over C$120, the complaint rate in our data is 9.6% across 334 reviews, against 30.3% under C$50 across 3,259 Review analysis.

What we didn’t like about the Dreame Pocket Pro

1. Only about 163 units a month in Canada — the biggest limitation on this review. The Laifen Air moves 534 and the Laifen SE Lite 448. With fewer Canadian owners, there are fewer long-term reviews, so we cannot tell you how a Dreame behaves at month twelve. Anyone claiming otherwise about this model is guessing Amazon.ca data.

2. BSR #52 — the weakest category ranking of any model we recommend. It ranks below every Laifen model in our coverage and below both Dyson Supersonics Amazon.ca data.

3. It costs C$60 more than the Laifen Air for 0.1 of a star. At about C$100 the Laifen Air is 4.5★. The C$60 difference buys dual voltage and an included diffuser — nothing else measurable Amazon.ca data.

4. Spare attachments will be harder to source in Canada. Laifen and Dyson both have broader Canadian retail presence. For a dryer with a proprietary diffuser, that matters if the attachment is lost Review analysis.

5. We have not tested it. Every measured row in this review reads “not yet tested”, because we will not estimate airflow, noise or dry time. That limit applies to every dryer we cover, and we say so on each one — see how we test.

Dreame Pocket Pro drying performance

What we can say: the Dreame Pocket Pro is a high-speed brushless dryer, which means it moves a large volume of air at a lower temperature rather than relying on a hot element. That is the same approach Laifen and Dyson use, and it is the right one for dense or long hair Manufacturer claim.

Why the approach matters. Airflow was the most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,585 mentions, and the complaint pattern runs one way: reviewers rarely complain a dryer is too powerful, they complain it is too weak for their hair. Underpowered dryers are the most common single reason reviewers describe returning one Review analysis.

What we cannot say: how fast it actually dries. We have not measured airflow velocity or dry time on a standardised swatch. When the unit completes our protocol, those numbers get published on the Lab Test Card and this review gets a new last-updated date.

Practical guidance: if your hair is thick or long and drying speed is your priority, the Laifen SE2 at about C$145 is specifically tuned for that buyer and costs C$16 less. The Dreame’s case rests on travel, not on power.

Dreame Pocket Pro heat and settings

Heat control is the second-largest complaint cluster in our dataset, so it is worth examining on any dryer.

  • The Pocket Pro uses a high-speed brushless motor, which generates less heat for the same airflow than a conventional element Manufacturer claim
  • Dyson’s Supersonic Nural takes heat control further with active heat sensing, which the Dreame does not claim Manufacturer claim
  • Temperature and overheating produced 590 negative mentions in our data, 54% of all heat-related comments Review analysis

The failure pattern in our data is hardware, not control logic. The severe outcomes we coded — smoke at 182 mentions with 96% negative, melting plastic at 64 with 89% negative — are component failures. Better heat control does not protect you from a cord that fails at the handle junction.

Two safety checks worth running on arrival regardless of the review you are reading: the ALCI plug should have a rectangular GFCI-style box, and the cord strain relief where it enters the handle should not flex easily. Cord and connector failure accounted for 417 mentions in our dataset, second only to complete stoppage at 601 — see how long hair dryers actually last.

Dreame Pocket Pro noise

Noise appears in 848 reviews in our dataset, 10.3% of the total, with 33% of mentions negative Review analysis.

Dreame does not publish a measured sound pressure figure at a stated distance Manufacturer claim, and neither does Laifen or Dyson. “Low noise” appears across this category without a number attached to it.

What we will publish: sound pressure at 30 cm and at 1 metre, against a recorded background level, using the same meter for every unit. Until that exists for the Pocket Pro, the honest answer is that we do not know how it compares — and neither does anyone else publishing a comparison without a meter.

Dreame Pocket Pro weight and handling

Weight is the third most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,318 mentions, and 73% of it is positive — buyers notice when a dryer is light Review analysis.

What is verifiable: the Pocket Pro is positioned as a compact, packable dryer rather than a full-size one Manufacturer claim. Size and storage was the most positively discussed topic in our entire dataset at 1,429 mentions and 74% positive, which is a genuine point in its favour for a travel dryer Review analysis.

Why weight matters more than it sounds. A hair dryer is held at arm’s length for five to fifteen minutes. Complaints in our data cluster around longer hair and longer sessions, so if your hair is long, weight should rank above peak airflow in your decision.

What we will publish: measured weight with the cord, and the hand-held section separately. Until then, treat every weight claim on any listing in this category as unverified.

Dreame Pocket Pro attachments and diffuser

This is the second concrete advantage over the Laifen Air, and it is not cosmetic.

  • The diffuser ships with the dryer rather than as a separate variant, so the fit is matched to the barrel Manufacturer claim
  • Our data shows 186 mentions of attachment problems with 57% negative, and “the nozzle keeps falling off” is the recurring phrasing Review analysis
  • One reviewer described a nozzle that had melted where it sat against the barrel Buyer feedback
  • Universal aftermarket diffusers fit no barrel precisely, which is the most likely route to the falling-off problem

The test to run on arrival: fit the diffuser, invert the dryer, and shake it gently ten times. Do that on day one, inside the return window. It takes thirty seconds and it is the single most common curly-hair complaint we found.

If you have curly or wavy hair, our curly hair guide covers which models suit that texture, and our diffuser guide explains how to use one without causing frizz.

Dreame Pocket Pro dual voltage and travel

This is the reason to buy this dryer, so it deserves its own section.

SituationWhat the Pocket Pro offers
Using it in CanadaStandard 120V operation
Europe, UK, AustraliaDual voltage, with a plug adapter Manufacturer claim
United StatesNo change needed
Hotel-supplied dryersLightweight and usually weak — carrying your own avoids this
Curly hair abroadDiffuser included, which hotel dryers never have

What a plug adapter cannot do. An adapter changes the shape of the plug, not the voltage. A single-voltage Canadian dryer plugged into a European 220–240V socket is damaged, sometimes immediately. A converter capable of running a hair dryer at 1,600W+ costs more than this dryer does.

The honest caveat: confirm the exact voltage range on the current listing before you travel. Models get revised, and we are working from the listing data we hold at a stated date. Our travel hair dryer guide covers the alternatives, including the Dyson Supersonic Travel at about C$400 and the Revlon RVDR5034F at about C$19.

Dreame Pocket Pro reliability and warranty

This is the section where we have to be least conclusive, and we would rather say so than fill the gap with a guess.

What the category data shows:

Failed out of the box0.8%
Durability mentions that were negative84%

Where the Pocket Pro sits. At about C$160 it is inside the better price band, and the 4.6★ rating from 252 buyers is consistent with that. That is the strongest reliability signal we can offer (Amazon.ca data, review analysis).

What we cannot tell you. With 163 units a month and 443 days on sale, there are not enough Canadian owners to distinguish a reliable product from a lucky early sample. The same limitation applies to every Laifen model — its newest listings are only four months old. If proven longevity is your priority, Dyson has by far the longest track record and a Canadian service network.

One structural advantage the Dreame does have: a brand-operated listing with a single seller. Warranty complaints were the second-largest cluster in our data at 610 negative mentions and 81% negative, largely driven by reseller listings where no one owns the claim. This listing has the same single-counterparty structure that Laifen uses Amazon.ca data.

Dreame Pocket Pro price and value

about C$160 buys you four things:

  1. Dual voltage — genuinely rare among high-speed dryers in Canada
  2. A matched diffuser — not an aftermarket part
  3. 4.6★, the joint-highest rating above C$120 in our dataset
  4. A brand-operated single-seller listing — one warranty counterparty

What C$60 less buys you instead: the Laifen Air at about C$100, at 4.5★ with 278 ratings and 534 units a month. Same high-speed brushless approach, no dual voltage, no diffuser as standard, and a larger Canadian ownership base.

What C$200 more buys you: the Dyson Supersonic Travel at about C$400 — universal voltage stated plainly, 310 Canadian ratings, a decade of product history and a Canadian service network.

Our honest read on value: the Pocket Pro is good value if you travel internationally at least once a year. If you do not, you are paying C$60 for a diffuser, and the Laifen SE2 at about C$145 is arguably the better buy for the same money because it is tuned for dense hair.

Read the comparison honestly. The Dreame wins on rating and on travel capability. It loses on price, on Canadian sales volume, and on the length of its track record. All four models sit in the same price band where our complaint rate is 9.6%, so none of them is disadvantaged on that measure.

Who should buy the Dreame Pocket Pro

Buy it if:

  • You travel internationally and want one high-speed dryer for home and abroad
  • You have curly or wavy hair and want a diffuser that is matched to the dryer rather than an aftermarket part
  • You want the highest-rated premium dryer in our Canadian dataset
  • You value a brand-operated listing with one seller and one warranty counterparty
  • about C$160 is within budget for a dryer you will keep for several years

Do not buy it if:

  • You never travel — the Laifen Air at about C$100 covers the same approach for C$60 less
  • Your hair is thick or long and drying power is your priority — the Laifen SE2 at about C$145 is tuned for that and costs less
  • Proven long-term reliability is your main criterion — Dyson has the track record and the service network
  • You want the largest Canadian ownership base to learn from — the Laifen SE Lite has 550 ratings against this model’s 252

Dreame Pocket Pro FAQ

Is the Dreame Pocket Pro worth it? Yes, if dual voltage matters to you. It is the joint-highest-rated dryer above C$120 in our Canadian dataset at 4.6 stars, it includes a diffuser, and it is sold through a brand-operated listing with a single seller. If you never travel, the Laifen Air at about C$100 delivers a similar high-speed approach for C$60 less.

Is the Dreame Pocket Pro dual voltage? Yes, and that is its main advantage over almost every other high-speed dryer sold in Canada. Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 785 mentions, and most Canadian dryers are 120V only. Confirm the exact range on the listing before you travel, since models are revised.

How does the Dreame Pocket Pro compare to the Laifen Air? The Dreame costs C$60 more at about C$160 against about C$100, and rates 0.1 stars higher at 4.6 against 4.5. What you get for the difference is dual voltage and a diffuser included as standard. If neither matters to you, the Laifen Air is the better value.

Does the Dreame Pocket Pro come with a diffuser? Yes. That matters more than it sounds, because attachment security is the most common curly-hair complaint in our data at 186 mentions and 57% negative. A diffuser that ships with the dryer is matched to its barrel diameter, which holds better than a universal aftermarket part.

Why does the Dreame Pocket Pro only sell about 163 units a month? Its price is the main reason. At about C$160 it sits above the Laifen Air at about C$100 and competes with entry Dyson pricing. Low Canadian volume is the honest limitation on this review: there are not yet enough long-term Canadian owners to judge reliability.

Is the Dreame Pocket Pro good for thick hair? It is a high-speed brushless dryer, so it moves air rather than relying on heat, which is the right approach for dense hair. But at about C$160 the Laifen SE2 is specifically tuned for thick or long hair and costs C$16 less, so compare those two before deciding.

Our verdict on the Dreame Pocket Pro

Recommended — for travellers, and for anyone who wants a diffuser included.

The Dreame Pocket Pro earns a recommendation on three things we can verify: 4.6★ from 252 Canadian ratings, which is the joint-highest above C$120 in our dataset; dual voltage, which almost no high-speed dryer sold in Canada offers; and a brand-operated single-seller listing, which gives you one counterparty if it fails.

What holds it back is evidence, not performance. At 163 units a month there are not enough Canadian owners to say how it behaves in year three, and we have not bench-tested it. We would rather state that than imply a confidence we do not have.

Buy it if you travel. If you do not, the Laifen Air at about C$100 is the better value and the Laifen SE2 at about C$145 is the better pick for dense hair.
